## Approved Plan:
# Add global button click-scale effect

## Context
The user wants a subtle "press" feedback on click for buttons — `transform: scale(0.97)` on `:active` — applied globally to all `<button>` elements, not just the shared shadcn-style `Button` component. This matches an existing pattern in the codebase: `src/components/ui/button.tsx` already has a press effect (`active:not-aria-[haspopup]:translate-y-px`, a 1px downward nudge) baked into its `cva` variant string, but that only covers buttons built from that component — not one-off buttons like `src/components/case-study/PillButton.astro`. A global rule in the site's base stylesheet catches everything.

## Approach
Add a `button:active` rule to the `@layer base` block in `src/styles/global.css` (that block currently runs from line 226–270 and already holds other global element-level rules like the `html { @apply font-sans; }` and `code { ... }` rules — this is the established place for "site-wide, not scoped to one layout" styling, per the existing comment on the `code` rule).

```css
@layer base {
  /* ...existing rules... */

  /* Subtle press feedback on click, site-wide — any real <button> element,
     not just ones built from the shadcn Button component. */
  button:active {
    transform: scale(0.97);
  }
}
```

### Notes / things to watch
- This only targets literal `<button>` elements via the CSS selector `button:active`. `PillButton.astro` renders an `<a>` (or similar) it won't be caught — need to check its markup; if it's not a real `<button>`, may need a follow-up (out of scope for this change unless confirmed).
- The shared `Button` component (`src/components/ui/button.tsx`) already applies `active:translate-y-px` via Tailwind. Adding a global `scale(0.97)` on top means shadcn-derived buttons would get **both** effects (translate + scale) stacking as a single `transform`, which is likely fine (translate-y-px is barely visible) but worth eyeballing in the browser once added, since it can look like an odd combined shift if the two clash visually.
- No token/variable needed for a single hardcoded `0.97` scale value — this matches the simplicity of the rest of the file's utility rules (e.g. the `code` block also uses hardcoded values, not tokens), so no change to the `@theme inline` section is needed unless the user wants this value reused/adjustable elsewhere later.

## Verification
1. Run the dev server (`bun run dev` per user's `bun` preference) and open the site locally.
2. Click various buttons across the site (nav, footer theme toggle, blog category filters if buttons, PillButton if it turns out to be a real `<button>`) and visually confirm the scale-down happens on `:active` (mouse-down) and reverts on release.
3. Toggle dark/light theme and confirm the effect looks correct in both (it should — `transform` isn't theme-dependent).
4. Run lint per user's standing preference ("Always lint work before we commit it") before considering this done.

Found it. `transition-all` is a Tailwind utility class — in Tailwind v4, utility classes are compiled into `@layer utilities`, and **Tailwind's layer order is `base` → `components` → `utilities`**, so `utilities` always wins over anything in `@layer base`, regardless of selector specificity. Your plain `button { transition }` rule in `@layer base` is losing to `.transition-all` in `@layer utilities` for every button built from the shared `Button` component — which is most buttons on the site (nav, footer, etc.).

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
This is one of the most common gotchas with Tailwind's `@layer` system: layer order, not specificity, decides the winner between rules of equal specificity that live in different layers. A single-class selector like `.transition-all` (specificity 0,1,0) sitting in `@layer utilities` beats a bare-element selector like `button` (specificity 0,0,1) in `@layer base` — normally the class would win on specificity alone anyway, but even if you wrote `button { transition: ... }` with `!important` inside `@layer base`, Tailwind's layers still resolve before that, so the safest fix is intercepting at the actual value Tailwind sets, not fighting it from outside.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

`transition-all` sets `transition-property: all` with Tailwind's default timing function and duration (`150ms` `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` — the `ease` Tailwind uses for `-all`/`-colors`/etc). Since `all` already includes `transform`, the shared `Button` component technically already has a transition — the transform *should* be animating there. If it's still instant on the buttons you're testing, they're likely not using the shared `Button` component at all (e.g. raw `<a>` styled to look like a button, or a plain `<button>` without those classes).

Found the actual bug. Line 46: `transition-colors` — this is a Tailwind utility that **only transitions color-related properties** (`color`, `background-color`, `border-color`, etc.), not `transform`. And critically, because it's an Astro-scoped `<style>` block plus a specific Tailwind utility class, it sets `transition-property: color, background-color, ...` explicitly — meaning `transform` is excluded from the transition list entirely for this button. Our global `button { transition: transform ... }` rule in `@layer base` loses to `.transition-colors` in `@layer utilities` (same layer-order issue as before), so `PillButton` never gets a transform transition at all — it just snaps.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
`transition-all` and `transition-colors` aren't "extra" vs "less" of the same thing — they set entirely different values for `transition-property`, and only one `transition-property` declaration can win per element. `transition-colors` explicitly lists `color, background-color, border-color, text-decoration-color, fill, stroke` — `transform` isn't in that list, so no amount of `transition-duration`/`ease` tuning elsewhere fixes it. The fix has to touch the actual `transition-property` list, not just add a competing rule.
